# Product context — HOF-GITHUB-123

Work item: `github:owner/repository#123` — Annotate short links

Source: revision `<REVISION>` (CHG-ANNOTATE-001 / SLI-ANNOTATE-001)

## Delivery outcome

A visitor can annotate a short link.

Verification:

- A note can be attached through the product surface.

Out of scope:

- Note editing.

## Implemented and related requirements

### FR-ANNOTATE-001 — FR-ANNOTATE-001 title

## Requirement
The product MUST attach notes to short links.
## Rationale
Notes make shared links understandable.
## Acceptance Scenarios
A note round-trips.

## Affected behaviour

### UC-ANNOTATE-001 — UC-ANNOTATE-001 title

## Goal
Annotate a short link with a note.
## Trigger
The visitor adds a note.
## Preconditions
A short link exists.
## Main Flow
1. The visitor submits a note for a short link.
## Alternative Flows
None.
## Failure Conditions
Invalid notes are rejected.
## Postconditions
The note is attached.

## Governing rules

### BR-VALID-URL-001 — Only well-formed absolute URLs are shortened

## Rule

The service shortens a URL only when it is a well-formed absolute web address.

## Rationale

A short link to a malformed address would fail for everyone who receives it.

## Examples

`https://example.org/a/very/long/path` is accepted; `not-a-url` is rejected.

## Exceptions

None.

## Domain language

### BC-SHORTENING — Shortening

## Responsibility

Everything about creating and resolving short links.

## Language

Short links, original URLs, resolution.

## Boundaries

Analytics, accounts and moderation are outside this context.

## External Relationships

None in this minimal example.

### TERM-SHORT-LINK — Short Link

## Definition

A compact, stable address issued by the service that redirects to exactly one original URL.

## Distinguish From

The original URL it points to, and a temporary redirect that may change targets.

## Usage

Created by shortening; shared by visitors; resolved on every visit.

## Constraints

### CON-NO-TRACKING — The service does not track visitors

## Constraint

The service stores no personal data about who creates or follows links.

## Rationale

A deliberate product boundary of this minimal example.

## Consequences

No analytics features can be built on visitor identity.

## Actors

### ACT-VISITOR — Visitor

## Purpose

A person who wants to share a long web address in a short, reliable form.

## Goals

Turn a long URL into a short one and trust that it keeps working.

## Responsibilities

Provides the URL to shorten; distributes the short link.

## Boundaries

Does not administer the service or see other visitors' links.

## Open questions

None.
